title: each Homebrew-released tool carries its own formula renderer (source-build or release-asset): devbin ships formula render and publish as a shared built-in, and its own command retires into it
body:
## The problem

The dev/opt/brew contract (docs/dev-opt-brew.md, T8) has every Homebrew-released tool render its formula, never type it, with a formula tool offering `render <tag> <out>` and `publish`. Each tool writes its own. devbin's is a project command in its own tree (bin/.devbin/cmd/formula), rendering a source-build formula from a template with the tag and its commit read from git. Another estate project carries a second, for a formula that installs signed release assets, filled from the release's SHA256SUMS. A third project is writing a third, for release assets and a cask. They share the hard parts: the tag read from git or from the release, never typed; the tap cloned, committed and pushed; the push behind a person's yes; Homebrew's measured quirks (a top-level url, no version line where brew derives it, 0755 on the keg's binaries); and, for release assets, the keg writing T3's manifest with `managed_by: brew`. A fix in one does not reach the others.

hv's lens for these rulings is no bespoke mechanism where an estate-ready one can exist, and 0226 hoisted the macOS app release the same way. Asked by another estate's dc on 2026-10-25, before its own renderer grows.

## Done when

1. devbin ships `formula` as a built-in with T8's verbs, `render <tag> <out>` and `publish`, in two modes chosen by project config:
   - **source**: a template in the project (default `packaging/homebrew/<tool>.rb`) with one placeholder for the tag and one for its commit, filled from git, refusing a missing or lightweight tag (what devbin's own command does now);
   - **assets**: the formula, and a cask where the project declares one, rendered from a release's version and the sha256 of each asset, read from the release's SHA256SUMS, with the keg laying the assets out under `libexec` and writing T3's manifest.
2. `publish` renders the newest release (by the release core's own rule under release.tag) into a temporary clone of the project's declared tap, commits and pushes it, behind `ask_person`, with no `--yes`. It writes nothing in the project's tree, and refuses a template with uncommitted changes.
3. devbin's own bin/.devbin/cmd/formula retires into the built-in: devbin's config declares source mode, and its tap publish and its cut's `after:` step run the built-in unchanged in effect.
4. The keys (mode, template, tap, assets and their names, the cask) are documented in lib/config.reference.yaml, each with a default where one is sound. A project's own `formula` command still wins, as for any built-in.
5. Arms: red on 593109bf first, then green, BSD and GNU, with the tree scans: each mode's render against a fixture release (a local bare tap and a stubbed gh, no network), the refusals, publish's ask, and devbin's own render byte-identical to what its retired command renders for v0.1.14. The full suite is green.
6. The issue and its arms name no project; devbin keeps no list of who uses it.

## Resolution

Fixed at a997339e and at dad27e48 (0227b, below), landed on landing suite 20261026-0642 at 261286d6, beside the public candidate's suite 20261026-0652: in both, every test ran and passed, the only skips were the standing environmental ones, and the errors seal was empty. cc built both in scratch clones, and vc landed them.

- **Done when 1.** devbin ships `formula` as an opt-in built-in, lib/cmd/formula (`commands.formula.enabled: true`), with T8's verbs, in the modes `formula.mode` chooses, source and assets. Both fill a template the project keeps (`formula.template`, default `packaging/homebrew/<name>.rb`), so a project's own Ruby -- desc, caveats, an install layout, a service block -- stays its own (design (B), vc's call).
  - **source**: exactly one `@@TAG@@` and one `@@REVISION@@`, filled from git, a missing or lightweight tag refused: devbin's own command's rule, moved whole.
  - **assets**: `@@VERSION@@`, from the tag through `release.tag`; `@@SHA256:<asset>@@`, exactly once per asset in `formula.assets` across the formula and the cask, read by its exact name from the release's sums file (`gh release download` on `formula.repo`, or `--sums <file>`), never computed here from a download; and exactly one of `@@INSTALL@@` or `@@FINISH@@`, the install body devbin generates: 0755 on each of `formula.bin`, T3's manifest under libexec (tool, version, source_commit, `managed_by: brew`, one `<sha256>  <path>` line per file sorted bytewise, itself left out), and a link in bin for each. A cask, where `formula.cask` names one, is rendered from the same release. `@@VERSION@@` may appear more than once, since a per-arch template needs it in each url (vc agreed).
  - In both modes a placeholder left after filling is refused by name, and a key the mode does not read is refused rather than ignored.
- **Done when 2.** `publish` renders the newest release, by the core's `--patch` rule under `release.tag`, into a temporary clone of the tap (`formula.tap`, default `homebrew-<name>` under the release repository's owner), commits and pushes it. It writes nothing in the tree, refuses an uncommitted template or cask, leaves a tap already carrying the render alone without asking, and otherwise names the tap and asks through `ask_person`, with no `--yes`. The formula and the cask go in one tap commit.
- **Done when 3.** devbin's bin/.devbin/cmd/formula and its help page are retired. devbin's config declares `formula: mode: source` and enables the built-in, and its render of v0.1.14 through the built-in is byte-identical to the retired command's (sha256 `fd73339ed3b4739a901fd170adc8dfff5c7af921ee990ac49d402417e3835faf` from both, rendered in real checkouts at 593109bf and on the build). The cut's `after:` line is unchanged. A `bin/devbin` after: line cannot ask a person, since the dispatcher drops the gate's mark (issue 0158), so the release core hands its after: commands `DEVBIN_RELEASE_CONFIRMED`, naming the tag, only when the confirm step was answered at its prompt and never under `--yes` (vc's ruling (1)), and publish takes it as the yes for the push the cut lists, for exactly that tag, saying so. A cut under `--yes` therefore publishes no formula, and its after row and docs/releasing.md say so; that is tighter than before, when the after step pushed with no yes at all. The mark is an environment variable a caller of the same user could set; this is accepted because the cut and the tap push are both the maintainer's own hand. lib/cmd/release's comment on after: commands that ask is corrected.
- **Done when 4.** The keys are one schema table in lib/config (`_DEVBIN_FORMULA_SCHEMA`: mode, name, template, tap, repo, sums, manifest, cask, assets, bin), documented in lib/config.reference.yaml, docs/configuration.md#formula and lib/pages/formula.md, each with its default where one is sound; `formula.mode` is validated. `cfg_formula_name` (lib/config) is the one derivation of the formula's name, `formula.name` else `project.name`, which the built-in asks and 0228's closing note will (hv's ruling A). A project's own `formula` command or `run:` still wins, as for any built-in.
- **Done when 5.** formula.bats, over the built-in, against a local bare tap and a stubbed gh, no network: each mode's render (assets with decoy names in the sums file and a cask), `--sums`, every refusal, publish's ask (yes, no, nobody), the cut's mark (its tag, another tag), the unchanged tap, and devbin's declaration; the generated install body run under plain Ruby, where ruby is installed, with brew's DSL stood in for: 0755 set, the manifest's header and a body equal to `sha256_files` over the keg, the link made. releasecut.bats' after: arms on a pty: published on the prompt's yes, a failing push reported, no formula under `--yes` on a terminal or with nobody at one. The arms that answer a prompt run through expect and are skipped where it is not installed. Red on 593109bf (v0.1.14): every new and changed arm fails there, on the built-in's absence. Green, each arm alone, BSD and GNU. A first targeted run, under molt-vc's GO of 2026-10-25 10:21Z, went red in helpers, contract, neutral, documentation, help and surfaces. Each was fixed: dc's scan findings (`gate_tty_flag` in lib/helpers as the one reading of whether a gate can reach a terminal, asked by gate_exec and publish; no raw sha256 tool outside lib/helpers; no tracker, estate count or ruling prose in user-read text; a reserved example domain; FORMULA in the documentation scan's schema extractor; awk where a pipe fed an early reader), formula in help's and surfaces' all-built-ins fixtures, and a page that names no `docs/` path. The re-run, under molt-vc's GO LIGHT of 2026-10-25 11:19Z, on 0227 rebased onto 0226b (1b748f0a): formula, releasecut, releasecore, config, dispatch, help, optin, surfaces, review, builtins, helpers, contract, neutral, documentation, readonlygit, harness, runlog and clean, each file alone, BSD then GNU, every arm ok in both, the only skips those the suites declare (no runner without a controlling terminal, require_command off CI). Critic leg: `intent critic shell --files <each changed file>` from the repo root, rc 0, no shell finding at severity warning or above; the other changed files asked nothing. Not proven here: a real `brew install` of an assets formula.
- **Done when 6.** The issue, the arms, lib/ and the page name no project; devbin keeps no list of who uses it.
- **0227b.** land220's landing pair of 2026-10-25 went red on vendoredmd.bats's wrap arm and its default-config prettier arm: lib/pages/formula.md's refusal lists and its See also were indented two spaces, which prettier rewrites and the wrap arm reads as hard-wrapped prose. 0227's targeted runs had carried neither vendoredmd nor workroom. 0227b puts the lists at the margin, as check.md's are, and See also in a four-space literal block, as the other pages set it, whitespace only (`git diff -w` is empty). Red on c320ba06 on exactly the wrap and default-config arms, BSD and GNU; green at its scratch commit 18e59ec1 across vendoredmd, helpers, contract, neutral, documentation, readonlygit, harness, workroom and help, each file alone, BSD and GNU, under molt-vc's GO of 2026-10-26 06:28Z, with workroom red only on 0229's lib/runlog lines, which 0229b fixed.
